result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.dominating_set()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find a dominating set for the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L22494-L22572){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.dominating_set(start_with=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} A dominating set `D` of a graph `G = (V, E)` is a subset of V such that every vertex not in `D` is adjacent to at least one member of `D`. This method uses a greedy algorithm that finds some dominating set, but not necessarily the minimum one. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [start_with]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node ID to start the algorithm from. If `None`, an arbitrary node is chosen. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs forming a dominating set. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the `start_with=` node doesn't exist in the graph. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(V + E)` greedy algorithm - space complexity: `O(V)` for tracking dominated nodes - not guaranteed to find the minimum dominating set (NP-hard problem) - every maximal independent set is a dominating set - related to but different from `domirank_centrality()` ## Examples {.doc-examples} On a random graph, the greedy algorithm produces some dominating set (not necessarily the smallest possible), which can be verified with `is_dominating_set()`: ::: {#a4f91d45 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_gnm_graph(n=100, m=200, seed=23) dom = graph.dominating_set() # Returns True: every node is either in the set or adjacent to a member graph.is_dominating_set(dom) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: In a star graph, the hub alone dominates every leaf, so starting the search there gives the smallest possible dominating set right away: ::: {#fd258abf .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_star_graph(10) # Hub with 9 leaves dom = graph.dominating_set(start_with=1) # Start from the hub # Returns 1 (just the hub) len(dom) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Every maximal independent set is also a dominating set (since any node not in the set must be adjacent to one that is), so the two methods often produce comparably-sized results: ::: {#4517da12 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_cycle_graph(8) dom = graph.dominating_set() ind = graph.maximal_independent_set(seed=23) # Compare the two set sizes (len(dom), len(ind)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (4, 3) ``` ::: :::
